key_insight: Secondary motions are ridge-locked, amplified large-scale motions whose strength governs coexistence with very-large-scale motions, while ridge spacing controls their location and persistence.
engineering_relevance: Ridge height and spacing offer design levers for tuning large-scale turbulence organization over patterned channel surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent open-channel flow over streamwise-aligned Gaussian ridges.
Variation of ridge height and spacing.
Proper orthogonal decomposition and conditional averaging of instantaneous motions.
evidence_signal: VLSMs were suppressed at ridge heights h ≥ 0.05δ and re-emerged at h = 0.025δ, while instantaneous secondary motions spanned approximately 2δ and filled the channel height across the tested geometries.
watch_item: The reported thresholds apply to the simulated open-channel configurations; transfer to other flow conditions or surface geometries requires validation.
paper_title: On the relation of secondary motions to large- and very-large-scale motions
